Reject unsupported document sources instead of dropping them.
`214-242`: ** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Heavy lift** **Reject unsupported document sources instead of dropping them.** The `document` decoder returns `nil` for `url`, `content`, and `file` sources. The InvokeModel route then sends the request without the attachment and returns success. Issue `#9308` requires a 4xx for these sources. The PR does not provide an exception. Add both. As per coding guidelines: “Case names must contain the provider keyword and model” and must end with ` - #`.

_Source: Coding guidelines_ ✅ Addressed in commit 0d5305b

**Issue:** **A text document whose content starts with `data:` now fails with a 400 instead of being sent.**

A `text` source puts the raw text in `Document.Source.Text`. `convertSingleBedrockMessageToBifrostMessages` copies that text unchanged into `FileData` (responses.go:5241). On the Converse egress, `materializeBedrockDocument` checks for a data URL with `strings.EqualFold(fileData[:5], "data:")` and returns `invalid document data URL` when the parse fails.

I reproduced it with a temporary overlay test (no files in the worktree were changed):

```
{"type":"document","source":{"type":"text","media_type":"text/plain","data":"Data: quarterly numbers"}}
→ converse err: failed to convert document in responses content block: invalid document data URL
```

Any text document that starts with `Data:`, `data:` and so on (a header line, a CSV column, a log dump) hits this. Before this PR the block was dropped; now the request fails. That is louder, but it is still wrong. The Anthropic InvokeModel egress (thinking on) sends the same block correctly.

Possible fixes:
- On the Bedrock → Bifrost side, hand the text over in an unambiguous form, e.g. `data:text/plain;base64,<b64>`. Check that the Anthropic egress still rebuilds a `text` source rather than a base64 one, because Anthropic only accepts base64 for PDFs.
- Or, in `materializeBedrockDocument`, fall back to literal text when the format is a text format and the `data:` prefix does not parse.

Either way, add a regression case with a `Data:`-prefixed text document.

**Suggestion:** **The same silent drop remains for the document shapes this case doesn't handle.**

In every one of these cases the block is still discarded and the client gets a 200 with no attachment, which is the failure #9308 reported:
- `url` sources (a common Anthropic shape; the probe confirms the block disappears on both egress paths)
- `content` sources and `file` sources
- a `media_type` that `bedrockDocumentFormat` doesn't recognise
- `base64` without `data`

Because `UnmarshalJSON` can return an error (the `tool_result` branch already does), consider rejecting these with a clear invalid-request error. A URL could also be carried through as a Bifrost `FileURL`, since `materializeBedrockDocument` already fetches and inlines it. If a silent drop is intended, say so in the doc comment and add a test that pins it.

**Suggestion:** **`citations` and `context` on the document block are dropped without notice.**

The probe shows both fields gone on both egress paths; `cache_control` survives. A client that sends `citations: {enabled: true}` gets a 200 response with no citations. On the Anthropic InvokeModel egress, the native block could carry citations unchanged.

Also, `normalizeBedrockFilename` turns an untitled document into `title: "document"` on the Anthropic egress, which then appears in the model's citation metadata. Consider keeping `Name` empty when `title` is absent and leaving the default to the Converse egress, which already applies it through `docNamer`.

At minimum, list these fields under "Not covered here" in the PR.

**Suggestion:** **The end-to-end test covers only the Converse egress and only the base64 source.**

When the InvokeModel ingress marks a request with `BedrockContextKeyAnthropicInvokeIngress` and thinking is on, `responsesUsesAnthropicInvokePath` sends it to `anthropic.BuildAnthropicResponsesRequestBody` instead. That path is not tested. Please add:
- the same test with `thinking` enabled and the context key set, asserting that the Anthropic body contains a `document` block with the original `source` type;
- a `text`-source case on both egress paths.

The harness case covers only the text source through the Converse path, so a regression in either of these would not be caught.

** Major** · **Maintainability & Code Quality** · **Quick win** **Use `providerUtils.MarshalSorted` for both test payloads.** Replace both new `sonic.Marshal` calls with `providerUtils.MarshalSorted`. As per coding guidelines: “When marshaling back out, always use `providerUtils.MarshalSorted` (never a raw `sonic.Marshal`/`json.Marshal`).” Also applies to: 3770-3770

Text beginning with `data:` remains literal text when passed through Converse and Anthropic. - **Tests** - Added coverage for document handling across request and response paths, including an end-to-end Bedrock InvokeModel request. Bedrock InvokeModel decoding now converts supported Anthropic document blocks with base64 or text sources and recognized media types. Responses conversion base64-encodes plain-text document content. Tests cover decoding, request conversion, egress, and an InvokeModel request. **Changes: Bedrock InvokeModel documents** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Decode Anthropic document blocks**

Tests cover top-level and nested block decoding, request conversion, unmarshalling benchmarks, and a text document in an InvokeModel request.| |**Preserve document sources during conversion**

Thanks for the careful review. Pushed a commit that fixes the blocking point.

**`data:`-prefixed text documents (blocking).** A `text` source went into `FileData` as raw text, so `Data: quarterly numbers` was read as a data URL by `materializeBedrockDocument` and failed with `invalid document data URL`. The Bedrock → Bifrost conversion now hands the text over as `data:text/plain;base64,<b64>`. The Converse egress decodes it into document bytes, and the Anthropic InvokeModel egress (`inlineTextDataURL`) rebuilds the original `text` source, so Anthropic never receives a base64 text document.

**Tests.** `TestInvokeDocument_TextSourceStartingWithDataPrefix` runs `Data: quarterly numbers`, `data:text/plain,not a url` and `DATA:x` through decode → Converse request and through the Anthropic request builder, asserting the document survives on both paths (Converse bytes decode to the original text; Anthropic keeps `source.type = "text"` with the original data). Without the `responses.go` change all three cases fail; with it they pass, and the whole `./providers/bedrock/...` package passes now.

**Not changed in this commit** (happy to do them here or in a follow-up, whichever you prefer): rejecting or carrying through `url`/`content`/`file` sources and unknown media types, `citations`/`context` on the document block, keeping `Name` empty for untitled documents on the Anthropic egress, and an e2e case with thinking enabled.
